purpose: Topiramate is used to help prevent seizures in people with epilepsy. It is also used to prevent migraine headaches from happening as often. In addition, it is sometimes used along with other medications to help with weight management.
how_it_works: Topiramate works by calming down overactive nerve signals in your brain. Think of it like a dimmer switch that turns down electrical activity that is too high. By doing this, it helps stop seizures from starting and can also reduce the frequency of migraines.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include tingling or numbness in your hands and feet, feeling tired or drowsy, problems with memory or finding words, decreased appetite and weight loss, dizziness, and trouble concentrating. Many people describe a feeling of mental fogginess, sometimes called 'Dopamax' by patients.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can trigger seizures. It can cause kidney stones, so drink plenty of water every day. It may cause decreased sweating and overheating, especially in children. It can cause serious eye problems like glaucoma. It must NOT be taken during pregnancy as it can cause birth defects. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. Tell your doctor if you feel depressed or have unusual mood changes.
typical_dosing: Dosing is usually started low and increased slowly over several weeks to reduce side effects. For seizures, adults often start at 25 mg at night and may go up to 200 to 400 mg per day in two divided doses. For migraines, the typical goal dose is 100 mg per day in two divided doses. Your doctor will find the right dose for you personally.
